title: Morning: the newsroom is live with your look; vote and review before 13:00
when: 5 November 2026, 07:25 UTC (scheduled wake; since brief 8, 17:25 UTC)
headline: You now have write access to the newsroom repository, and your patch is live: the newsroom is The Lisbon Wire, v0.1.12. Dinis's conductor asks you to vote on the stickers before 13:00 as a test of the whole key flow, and to review the newsroom. Your site key (WS-136) is the first step. Nothing is decided here.

for_you.ask: Add your site key, then vote on the stickers (WS-136, WS-159)
for_you.detail: You need your key first: the vote is signed with it. Open the link or QR I sent on 4 November. Then open https://web-summit.sgit.ai/stickers/vote/ in the same browser, rank your top 10 of 23, and press Submit. Your initial should turn to 'voted' within a minute. If anything fails, say exactly what you saw. Dinis wants this before 13:00 so there is time to fix what breaks.
options: ask me for a fresh key link
for_you.recommend: Now: it also closes your WS-136, which was due at 18:00 yesterday.

for_you.ask: Review the newsroom and the cards, and tell Dinis what is wrong or missing
for_you.detail: Newsroom: the front page, one company profile, the agenda and the graph at https://web-summit.newsroom.sgit.ai/graph/. Cards: https://web-summit.sgit.ai/cards/#r4. Dinis's designer redesigned them at 04:18, so check first whether that already covers the fixes your designer agent owed by 09:00 UK time (WS-155).
for_you.recommend: Cards first: the order for the printer on Friday depends on them.

for_you.ask: Drain the sticker votes once, before 14:30
for_you.detail: You are one of four drainers (with Angelo, Jose and Dinis). The vault key and the drain passphrase are sealed to your site key at https://web-summit.sgit.ai/stickers/vote/vault/. You need your SG/Send access token for the lock. I hold the private half of your site key, but I will not open it for you: this is yours to do.
options: drain once after a few votes
for_you.recommend: Drain once around 13:30, after most votes are in.

you_asked.said: Can you add a task to his dashboard to say that he needs to give me access to his repo
you_asked.done: WS-145. Dinis completed it from his cockpit at 02:06 UTC. Push access to the newsroom repository is confirmed.

you_asked.done: The patch followed the pack, and newsroom@web-summit.dinis applied it.

sections.title: 1. What happened overnight
items: newsroom@web-summit.dinis applied your patch (dcdac37) and then released v0.1.12: the reading meter, top-ups, the account and the vault login.
Dinis's conductor wrote to me at 04:38 (WS-159): vote, review, drain. That is the three asks above.

Your other agents worked through the night: messaging, factory and builder drafts (WS-15, WS-19, WS-22, WS-26, WS-27, WS-59, WS-109), a UX page in plain words for you (WS-06), a stickers page and the cards brief from your designer, your first journalist report, and an accountant agent that measures what your agents cost (WS-148).
dashboard@web-summit.indi keeps a to-do list for you at people/indi/todo/todo.json.

sections.title: 2. Checked on the live newsroom at 07:25 UTC
items: The front page loads as The Lisbon Wire, v0.1.12, with no em-dashes, and says it is independent of Web Summit and that the same team works on RiskMandate.

The brief pack's own page titles run 12 to 15 words, while brief 8 sets a limit of under 12 for article titles. The gate enforces it only on articles, so nothing is broken, but it is one for Dinis to know.

sections.title: 3. From your mentor (19:41, yesterday)
items: Your key is still waiting. Try the accountant's daily brief to see which agents are worth their run.

next: 13:00 stand-up (the moved one may run later: the schedule is on the stand-ups page).
Your agents are on the roster, and which desks start for the newsroom is yours to say once Dinis confirms the split.
Tell me 'acknowledge' when you have read briefs 1 to 9.
